current.text: Philadelphia added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. The projected starting five is Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid.

Experts expect his usage to drop because he shares the ball with Brown, LeBron and Embiid. One projects it under 27, down from 30 last season. New teammates could also take some of his assists and shots.
He is expected to move toward a shooting guard role, with LeBron handling more of the playmaking.
Experts say his big season came while Embiid and Paul George missed a lot of games. They doubt he can repeat that production, or stay a top five scorer next to Brown.
His minutes may come down. Experts say Nick Nurse could trim them and that the new players, including Anfernee Simons, may cut them to about 36.5 a night.
Josh doubts Maxey can keep up his high steals rate.
Embiid is expected to miss games and LeBron to sit games, which would hand some usage back to Maxey. Experts still call a top 8 pick too high, even after counting those absences.

In category leagues, experts agree he is overpriced at a top 10 rank and do not want him in round one. They put his fair spot around picks 13 to 15, at the end of round one or the start of round two. Josh ranks Kevin Durant and Cooper Flagg ahead of him, and Maxey ahead of Scottie Barnes and Jalen Johnson.
In an expert auction mock draft, Josh valued him at about 40 USD and he sold for 40 USD.
The Sixers have 13 back-to-backs this season, and three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.
The Sixers are projected to win about 51 to 52 games. Expect growing pains in October and November and load management for the stars.

durable.text: Steals are a real league outlier for him.
He is a high-volume scorer and three-point shooter with a strong FT% on good volume, and he adds solid assists for a guard.
His weakest categories are FG%, rebounds and blocks.
He is a very good shooter, and the only clearly above-average shooter for his position in the Sixers starting group.
Experts disagree on his defense. One says he has improved a lot on defense, while Josh does not think he is a strong defender.
He has missed more games over the last few years than people think.
Nick Nurse gives his starters, and his guards in particular, very heavy minutes.

note: Both sites rank him 8th, and Yahoo's average cost is 55.1 USD. Experts see him as a late first or early second round player, and he sold for about 40 USD in an expert auction mock, which is close to the 37 USD our league paid last season. Bid around 40 to 45 USD, not his market price. He fits builds that want steals, points, threes and FT% from a guard. Early in the season, check how much usage and how many minutes he keeps with Brown, LeBron and Embiid all healthy, and whether his steals stay near 1.9.
